clue.text: Stay after passport centre makes a bit of a mess

indicators.note: the stay word comes after the passport piece, so it follows it in the answer
the centre of the eight-letter word passport is its middle two letters

parts.note: the travel document, whose middle letters are taken
to lodge somewhere is to stay there

explanation.surface: A traveller warns that overstaying past passport control ends in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only orders the pieces: the stay word follows the centre of passport.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge is a blot or smear, a small messy patch of something spilled.

clue.text: Water-based dish from France is high level

indicators.note: in this down clue the water sits at the base, below the dish

parts.note: plat is French for dish; 'from France' also makes water the French eau
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A French dish cooked in water turns out to be top-class cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from France' governs both words: both the dish and the water are French.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high flat ground, and also a stable level that something reaches.

clue.text: Chemical that removes hard bit from leather

indicators.note: the hard bit is taken away from the leather word

parts.note: oxhide is leather made from an ox's skin
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tanning agent strips the tough part out of a hide.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element, like rust.

clue.text: Trojan worker provides good support

parts.note: a rafter is a beam supporting a roof

explanation.surface: A tireless labourer offers good backing.
explanation.walkthrough: To work like a Trojan is to work very hard; a grafter is British for a hard worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A grafter is someone who toils diligently, a hard worker.

clue.text: Former pupils gather pine to make shapes

indicators.note: the former pupils gather the pine word into their midst, so it goes inside them

parts.note: OBs are old boys, former pupils of a school
to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Old schoolmates collect pine wood to make some shapes in a craft session.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine reads as the tree but is the verb meaning yearn. OB, old boy, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblongs are rectangles, a family of geometric figures longer than they are wide.

clue.text: Cooked up plot to acquire fossil fuel

indicators.note: the plot acquires the fuel, taking it inside

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
oil is a fossil fuel

explanation.surface: A conspiracy is hatched to seize oil reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked up' suggests scheming, but here it is literal heating in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiled up means heated in bubbling water, a cooking method.

clue.text: Great activity that led to finished Verdi composition

parts.note: something over is finished

indicators.note: the letters of Verdi are composed into a new arrangement

parts.note: the opera composer's name, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A frenzy of work led to the completion of a Verdi opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdrive is a state of intense activity, as in going into overdrive.

clue.text: Upstanding Scandinavian infiltrates work unit producing small bomb

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the whole is read from the bottom upwards
the Scandinavian gets inside the work unit

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
a Dane is from Denmark

explanation.surface: An honest Scandinavian spy infiltrates a squad that makes small bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' looks like praise for the Dane, but it reverses the whole construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small hand-thrown explosive device.

clue.text: Basic directions for what you are doing!

definitions.meaning: the two fundamental orientations of a crossword's entries
the solver is filling a grid in both of those directions right now

explanation.walkthrough: A self-referential clue: the answer names the two ways crossword entries run.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword clues are grouped under the two headings for horizontal and vertical entries.

clue.text: Artist starts to date all Lowry's images

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words, their opening letters, are taken in turn

parts.note: four words whose opening letters are used

explanation.surface: An art historian notes when a famous painter began dating all of Lowry's pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowry is a red herring: L. S. Lowry painted northern English industrial scenes, but the answer is the Spanish surrealist.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter famous for melting clocks.

clue.text: Crime heads manipulated old scientist

indicators.note: the letters of crime heads are handled and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as the raw material

explanation.surface: Gang bosses distorted the work of some ancient scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes of Syracuse was the ancient Greek mathematician and inventor of the eureka story.

clue.text: Talk again about environmentally damaging contributor to agricultural growth

parts.note: re, as in a letter heading, means concerning

parts.words: environmentally damaging contributor to agricultural growth
parts.note: peat is dug for compost to help crops grow, but its extraction destroys bogs and releases carbon

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth a second time on a fertiliser that harms the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat something is to say it once more, to reiterate a remark.

clue.text: Add too much to sketch and get a negative balance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to exaggerate in drawing, putting too much into a picture
second meaning: to take more from a bank account than it holds

explanation.surface: An artist overdoes a drawing and ends up in the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two meanings; the first is the rarer artistic sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both exaggerating a depiction and withdrawing beyond the funds in one's account.

clue.text: Posh daily in top class city

indicators.note: the posh and daily pieces sit in the top-class word

parts.note: the best is the top class of anything
U is the old label for upper-class usage
a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char

explanation.surface: A smart daily newspaper is found in a first-class city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' suggests a newspaper, but in British usage a daily or char is a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital of Romania, a European metropolis.

clue.text: Uneven treatment of most Irish

indicators.note: giving the words a treatment works them over into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as the raw material

explanation.surface: A complaint that most Irish people get inconsistent treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit or miss means erratic or haphazard, sometimes succeeding and sometimes not.

clue.text: Scandal I believe is somewhat defamatory …

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: a libel is a defamatory statement

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying across them

parts.note: the answer lies across the last letter of the first word, the I, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone opines that a scandal is rather defamatory, the ellipsis carrying on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of the first word and into the next two.
explanation.definitionFit: A libel is a published statement that unjustly damages a person's reputation.

clue.text: … when copied thus?

definitions.meaning: the surface continues the previous clue: a libel is defamatory when written and copied
cryptically, the mark used to show something is copied from the line above

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a defamatory remark becomes worse when it is reproduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The ditto mark, two small commas, means 'the same as above', exactly the way a copy is marked in a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, written as a mark under an item that is repeated.

clue.text: Hot lines? Quite the opposite

parts.note: in means fashionable, as hot does
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether these are hot lines, and answers no.
explanation.definitionFit: The inverse is the reverse or contrary of something, its opposite.

clue.text: A gel NASA developed includes iodine for pain relief

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the iodine symbol inside them
the letters of a gel NASA are worked up into a new form

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter as the raw material
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Space scientists come up with an iodine gel that soothes pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for the absence or relief of pain, as from painkillers.

clue.text: Dead centre of Gibraltar approached from the side

parts.note: the late someone is someone dead
the middle three letters of the nine-letter word Gibraltar

explanation.surface: The very middle of the Rock was approached sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead centre' looks like one phrase meaning exact middle; split it into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to or coming from the side, as in a lateral pass.

clue.text: Drink that did for group when Mike left

parts.note: iced is slang for killed, did for

indicators.note: the Mike letter has left the group

parts.note: a team is a group of people
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A gangster tale where a drink finished off the gang once Mike had gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is a chilled tea beverage, a summer drink.

clue.text: Go, after throwing out rug

indicators.note: the go word comes after the jumbled piece
the letters of out are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: the word out itself, letter for letter, is jumbled
to go is to urinate, to pee

explanation.surface: A command to leave once the carpet has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' is slang for a wig, not a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A toupee is a hairpiece covering a bald patch, jokingly called a rug.

clue.text: Ask too much of tyrant, when America becomes Republican

indicators.note: the clue reads backwards: the answer becomes the tyrant word when its America letter becomes the Republican letter, so here that swap is undone

parts.note: an overlord is a domineering ruler

explanation.surface: A political jibe about a despot whose America turns Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the instruction in reverse: the answer turns into the tyrant when A changes to R, so build it from the tyrant with R changed to A.
explanation.definitionFit: To overload someone is to burden them beyond capacity, to demand too much.

clue.text: Check alien showing a means to gain entry

parts.note: to tick an item is to check it off
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A bouncer checks an alien's credentials at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket is the pass or voucher that admits its holder to an event or vehicle.

clue.text: Name for flowering plant with no root

indicators.note: in this down clue the root is the bottom, the final letter, which is cut off

parts.note: the cosmos is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A gardener is asked what to call a flowering plant without roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmo is a man's first name, short for Cosimo.

clue.text: Second rate shower might collectively display intelligence

parts.note: B is a second-class grade, as in B-movie
a shower is a spell of rain
the noun might, meaning strength or power

explanation.surface: A useless bunch of people might, as a group, show some brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is British slang for a hopeless group of people, and 'might' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainpower is mental capacity, the cleverness of a person or group.

clue.text: Swiftlet regularly seen on this place

indicators.note: every other letter of swiftlet is taken at a steady interval, starting from the first

parts.note: the bird's name supplies its first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports a little swift often spotted at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, the spot where something is or happens.

clue.text: Clear material picked up in accordance with plans

indicators.note: words picked up are heard, so these pieces are taken by their sound

parts.note: per specs: per means according to, and specs, short for specifications, are detailed plans

explanation.surface: A builder notes that transparent sheeting was ordered exactly to the drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: Perspex is the British trade name for acrylic sheet, what Americans call Plexiglas.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspex is a tough transparent plastic used in place of glass.

clue.text: Capital ensemble established in island has not been successful

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: an also-ran is one who has not been successful

indicators.note: the orchestra is set up inside the island

parts.note: Aran is an island group off western Ireland, also an island off Scotland
the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, a band from the capital

explanation.surface: An orchestra from the capital set up on an island and flopped.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a loser, originally a horse that finished unplaced in a race.
